title: All Rested Up?
dateline: A ruined rooftop, the same night.
mood: Night on a broken roof. Two rivals, too tired to fight, finally say what they mean.

hero.alt: Layla on a rooftop at night, her face smudged, her pink twin tails blowing in the wind.

segs.t: The roof had lost its north parapet. Layla sat on the south one with her boots over a two-story drop. Below, the rescue crews’ floodlights went up the dark avenue in pairs and stopped at each heap of rubble.
A medic had taped her cheek and wrapped her left forearm in gauze. She could not remember being cut.
Fanny had come up the stairs a quarter hour ago. “Mind if I stand?” she had said, and stood. Now she was at the broken edge with one hand taped. Neither of them had said anything useful.
Layla’s wristband buzzed.
“Roger,” she said. “Professor Joe’s awake. Two ribs and the shoulder. He wants to know if the girl got out.”
“She got out.” Fanny did not turn. “I left her behind a van. Her mother was running to her.”
Layla typed
Yes
and sent it. From the side street came a thin sound that had not stopped since dusk. She listened to everything else very hard instead.
“Well, I’ll admit you’ve got skill.” She said it to the avenue, not to Fanny.
“Thanks.”
“It’s an assessment. Don’t get used to it.”
“All right,” said Fanny.
Layla had meant to say something else. “You know, we’d probably get along if you weren’t so competitive all the time.”
“I could say the same of you.”
Layla opened her mouth to say that was unfair. She looked for the unfair part and could not find it.

media.alt: Fanny in profile against the dark city, her cheek smudged: I could say the same of you.
Close on Layla's eye, narrowed in annoyance.

segs.t: “... I have an elder brother ...” Fanny said it to the dark too. “An incredible fighter who I respect above anyone else. His name is Tigreal.”
Layla waited for the part about herself. It did not come.
“I’d longed to join him on the battlefield since I was just a kid. But the thing is.”

Fanny’s taped hand closed and opened. “I could never quite reach his level... I’d think... Maybe if I just gave it my all in each training, kept on improving... I’d be good enough to fight alongside him one day.”

media.alt: Fanny stands at the edge of the roof with her blade, looking away, while Layla sits below her: I have an elder brother.
Fanny, a hand at her cheek, before the dark outline of her elder brother.

segs.t: She was never looking down on me,
thought Layla.
She was looking past me, at him.
The shouted offer, the invitation at the drill hall door, the throw with the promise to teach it: every one had been an offer. Layla had filed each as an insult.
And that afternoon Fanny had answered “No!” to her face, out loud, in front of an Ender. Layla could not remember the last time she had told anyone she could not do something.

That left the grudge. It had been a good engine. It had kept her in the VR Battlefield until two and got her up before five. Its target stood on a broken roof talking about her brother. She would need a new reason to get up.
She tried three ways to say it. All three sounded like losing. The fourth sounded like an order, and an order was not asking.
She slid off the parapet, faced Fanny’s back, and spoke the way she spoke to her drones.
“All rested up?”

media.alt: Layla looks back over her shoulder at Fanny, saying nothing.
Layla, with a small smile: All rested up?

segs.t: Fanny turned around.
“If so, let’s get back to our training!”
“Huh?” Fanny stared. “Since when were we training?”

media.alt: On the ruined rooftop Layla stands by the parapet with her cannon while Fanny faces her, arms crossed.

segs.t: “Since right now!” Layla was smiling and had not agreed to it. Fanny was too.
“We’ve gotta get stronger,” they said together. “After all, we’re the protectors of all humanity.”
Neither had planned it.

media.alt: Layla raises her cannon to the night sky with a smile, and Fanny smiles behind her.

segs.t: Layla went first. She climbed onto the parapet and dropped into the dark street, and her boots jarred her to the teeth. Fanny had thrusters and could have beaten her down by a full second. She jumped instead, and landed a step behind.
